title: AI foundation model choice and false positive variation in Anti Money Laundering transaction screening — reproducibility archive
description: Reproducibility archive for the Discover Artificial Intelligence manuscript "AI foundation model choice and false positive variation in Anti Money Laundering transaction screening". From a frozen corpus of 12,120 screening calls (12,000 by design) over five zero-shot foundation models and a 600-case FATF-anchored battery, it regenerates every headline number offline and deterministically at zero cost: per-model false-positive rates spanning 2.3% to 85.7%, the cross-model spread with cluster-bootstrap intervals, Cochran's Q (585.0364, p = 2.683e-125) with Bonferroni-corrected pairwise exact McNemar tests, the aggregation-rule sensitivity across five tie policies and four deployable single-call configurations (spread 77.7 to 85.3 percentage points), the prevalence sweep, and the non-LLM baselines. Two independent runs are byte-identical.
notes: Code released under MIT (see LICENSE); data, analysis outputs and text under CC-BY-4.0. Reproduce with: bash reproduce.sh. Offline, no API keys, no network access required.
